display.purpose: KPI values on stat cards and scoreboards. Short numbers only (1-4 digits). Never wraps.

headline.purpose: Hero title and page title overlays. Used once per surface.

title.purpose: Card section headings at 16px; list item primary text at 14px. The workhorse heading.

body.purpose: Prose descriptions, search hints, empty-state messages. Capped at 65ch.

label.purpose: Stat labels, chip text, tag text. Uppercase, tight tracking. Never sentence case.

shadows.name: ambient-low
shadows.purpose: League tiles and context toggles on hover. Light diffuse lift.

shadows.name: ambient-mid
shadows.purpose: Hero card and home stat cards. Deeper but still soft.

shadows.name: accent-glow
shadows.purpose: Player avatar component only. Tinted shadow.

shadows.name: elevated
shadows.purpose: H2H selected player cards. The highest elevation; signals a picked state.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for state transitions (hover, focus, active). 200ms duration.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Exit animations and card dismissals. 150ms duration.

motion.name: duration-fast
motion.purpose: Micro-interactions: hover on/off, focus ring, chip toggle.

motion.name: duration-standard
motion.purpose: Card hover lift, tab switches, menu transitions.

narrative.overview: Like the pre-printed match card a player fills in before stepping to the table: structured, compact, and honest. Every inch of the surface earns its place. Numbers sit in tidy grids. Labels are short, weighty, and unambiguous. There is no decoration — only data arranged so you find what you need before the next serve. The system serves players between matches, league enthusiasts scrolling standings, and tournament organizers cross-referencing records. All on mobile, often in sports halls under mixed fluorescent light. The design answers this with high contrast, a single warm red accent, and typography that stays readable from 12px up.
keyCharacteristics: One accent, used sparingly on primary actions and selection states
System sans-serif throughout — native feel, no display type
Subtle warm tint to every neutral, even in dark mode
Flat surfaces at rest; shadows appear only on hover or selection
Pill-shaped everything: buttons, chips, result indicators, league filters
Dense-but-readable information layouts: 2-column grids, compact stat chips, form pills

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Match Red appears on at most 10% of any screen's surface area. The rest is structural gray. If a second saturated color appears, something is wrong.

rules.name: The Win/Loss Rule
rules.body: Never convey match outcome through color alone. Win pills include 'W' text and green background; loss pills include 'L' text and red background. A color-blind viewer always has the letter.

rules.name: The Scale Ratio Rule
rules.body: Adjacent hierarchy steps differ by at least 1.25× in size or two weight grades. A 12px label next to a 13px body is a flat scale; fix it.

rules.name: The System Stack Rule
rules.body: The system font stack is the only stack. No web fonts, no display/body pairing, no Google Fonts import.

rules.name: The Flat-At-Rest Rule
rules.body: A surface has no box-shadow in its default state. Shadows appear only as a response to interaction (hover, focus-visible) or selection (.active).

dos: Do use Match Red on at most 10% of any screen. The restraint is the point.
Do use the system font stack for every element. No web fonts, no display pairings.
Do pair every color-coded indicator with a text label, letter, or icon so color-blind users never lose meaning.
Do keep surfaces flat at rest. Add shadow only on hover, focus, or selection.
Do use pill shapes (999px radius) for chips, filter toggles, result indicators, and count badges.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: disable all transitions and shadow changes when the user requests it.
Do provide skeleton loading states for data sections, not centered spinners in empty space.
donts: Don't use a generic SaaS dashboard aesthetic — no blue sidebars, no hero-metric templates.
Don't use sports-betting neon accents, flashing elements, or overstimulating data feeds.
Don't use enterprise data-warehouse density: gray-on-gray chrome, massive tables, information overload.
Don't use flashy mobile game tropes: over-animated transitions, gamification badges, reward popups.
Don't use a border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't wrap everything in nested cards. A card inside a card is always wrong.
Don't use modal dialogs as a first resort. Inline expansion handles most cases on mobile.
